hands.description: Pungs of 2s and 4s with kongs of 6s and 8s, all in a single suit of your choice.
A pair of 2s, pungs of 4s and 6s, a kong of 8s, and a second pair of 8s — the 8s are split across two suits, the rest follows them.
Pairs and pungs trade places: a pung of 2s, a pair of 4s, a pung of 6s, a pair of 8s, and a kong of 4s in the second suit.
Concealed. Every even rank appears twice over: a pair in one suit and a pung or pair in the other — pairs of 2s, 4s, 6s and 8s with pungs of 2s and 6s woven in.
A pair of flowers opens the hand, then a pung of 2s, a kong of 4s, a pung of 6s and a pair of 8s across two suits.
Pungs of 1s and 3s with kongs of 5s and 7s, all in one suit — the odd mirror of the first Even Numbers hand.
Four pungs — 1s, 3s, 5s and 7s — split across two suits, closed out by a pair of 9s.
A pung of flowers, a pair of 1s, a pung of 9s, and 5s doing double duty — a kong in one suit and a pair in the other.
Concealed. Pairs of every odd rank across two suits, a hidden pung of 3s in the second suit, and one lone flower.
Kongs at both ends of the odd ranks — 1s in one suit, 9s in the other — with pungs of 3s and 5s in between.
The bottom stair in one suit: pungs of 1s and 2s climbing to kongs of 3s and 4s.
The same stair near the top of the suit: pungs of 5s and 6s, kongs of 7s and 8s, one suit throughout.
A run of 2 through 6 that changes suits halfway: pungs of 2s and 3s in one suit, pungs of 4s and 5s plus a pair of 6s in another.
A five-rank run, 3 up to 7, that grows as it climbs: pairs of 3s and 4s, pungs of 5s and 6s, a kong of 7s — all one suit.
A pair of flowers alongside a 3-to-6 run of pungs, the run switching suits between the 4s and the 5s.
Concealed. Pairs marching 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 across two suits, and a hidden kong of 6s in the first suit to make fourteen.
One rank, every suit: kongs of the same number in two suits and a pung of it in the third — shown here with 7s — plus a pung of flowers.
Two ranks share the work: pungs of 3s in two suits, pungs of 8s in the same two suits, and a pair of 3s in the third suit.
The same number konged in all three suits — shown with 1s, any rank works — and a pair of flowers to finish.
Concealed. Nothing but pairs: the same two ranks paired in every suit — 6s and 9s as shown — plus a pair of flowers.
A pung of every wind — North, East, South and West — finished with a pair of one dragon (red shown; any dragon works).
Kongs of Norths and Souths, a pung of green dragons, a pair of red dragons, and one lone West wind waiting for its match.
A pung of each dragon — green, red and white — with a pung of Norths and a pair of Easts beside them.
Number tiles hold the ends — pungs of 2s and 8s in one suit — while two different dragon pungs and a pair of Norths fill the middle.
Concealed. A pair of every wind, a pair of red dragons, a hidden pung of green dragons, and a single flower.
hands.notation: NN EE WW SS DD DDD F

hands.description: A quint of 5s — four natural tiles plus at least one joker — with pungs of 3s and 4s in the other suit, a pair of 9s and a flower.
The same rank twice over: a quint of 7s in one suit (one joker minimum) and a kong of 7s in another, with a pung and pair of 2s split the same way.
Two quints at once — 1s in one suit, 9s in another — so at least two jokers are committed before the pair of 6s and pair of flowers are even considered.
A quint of one dragon (green shown) — four natural dragons plus a joker or two — flanked by pungs of Norths and Easts, a pair of 8s and a flower.
Concealed. Seven clean pairs: six number pairs, each in a different suit from its neighbours, and a pair of flowers. No joker can help anywhere in this hand.
Concealed. Five odd singles scattered across the suits, pairs of Norths, Easts, 4s and flowers, and one lone white dragon.
Concealed. One of each wind standing single — North, East, West, South — with pairs of red dragons, 2s, 4s, 6s and flowers behind them.
hands.notation: N E W S DD 22 44 66 FF

hands.description: Concealed. The hardest hand on the card: twelve single tiles — every rank once across the suits, a North, an East and a green dragon — and only the flowers paired.
A full kong of flowers leads, with pungs of 2s and 3s in one suit and a kong of 4s in another.
Five flowers at once — a pair and a pung of them — beside pungs of 5s and 6s, a pair of 7s and a single 8.
The whole bouquet: all eight flowers, shown as two kongs, with pungs of 9s in two suits to round out the fourteen.
Pungs of 1s and 9s in two suits, and a pair of 1s in the third — nothing but the two ends of the suits.
Crossed bookends: a kong of 1s and a pung of 9s in one suit, a kong of 9s and a pung of 1s in the other.
A pung of flowers, pungs of 1s and 9s in one suit, a kong of 1s in the second suit, and one last single 9.
Concealed. Pairs of 1s and 9s in every suit, plus a pair of flowers — seven pairs, all bookends.

card.label: Practice Card — an original training card, not the official National Mah Jongg League card

notationKey.C: concealed only — the whole hand must be built without calling any tile
notationKey.D: a dragon of one kind (the kind is named in the hand's groups and description)
notationKey.X: exposures allowed — groups may be shown on your rack as you call them
notationKey.digits: a group of number tiles of that rank (e.g. 444 = a pung of 4s)
notationKey.jokers: Jokers are never printed in a pattern. A joker may stand in for a tile only inside a group of three or more (pung, kong, quint) — never as a single and never in a pair. A quint (five of a kind) always needs at least one joker, because only four natural copies of any tile exist.

card.origin: Every hand on this card was invented for Open Mahjong from the pattern grammar of American mahjong (see generation-record.md). No published card was consulted.

sections.blurb: Hands built only from the even ranks — 2, 4, 6 and 8. A gentle place to start: the tile pool is small, so discards are easy to track.
sections.name: Even Numbers

sections.blurb: Hands built only from the odd ranks — 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9. Same idea as Even Numbers with one more rank in play.
sections.name: Odd Numbers

sections.blurb: Staircases of neighbouring ranks, like 3-4-5-6, in one suit or split across two. Runs reward keeping flexible middle tiles early.
sections.name: Consecutive Runs

sections.blurb: The same rank repeated in suit after suit. You are hunting one or two ranks in every suit at once, so every copy anyone discards matters.
sections.name: Like Numbers

sections.blurb: Hands that lean on the honor tiles — the four winds and the three dragons — with number tiles in a supporting role.
sections.name: Winds & Dragons

sections.blurb: Every hand here contains at least one quint: five of a kind. Only four natural copies exist, so each quint is also a lesson in spending a joker.
sections.name: Quints

sections.blurb: No group larger than a pair, and jokers can never be used — a joker cannot stand in a pair or alone. Concealed only, and the hardest hands on the card.
sections.name: Singles & Pairs

sections.blurb: Our own family: hands that spend the eight flowers in earnest — flower kongs, flower pungs, and in one hand the whole bouquet. (A family invented for this card.)
sections.name: In Bloom

sections.blurb: Our own family: hands built only from the two ends of the suits, 1s and 9s — the tiles players throw away early and regret late. (A family invented for this card.)
sections.name: Bookends

tileSet.note: In the hand patterns below, suits are relative: suit 0, 1 and 2 mean 'one suit', 'a second suit' and 'a third suit'. Which physical suits you use is your choice at the table; what matters is which groups share a suit and which do not.

card.title: Open Mahjong Practice Card

valueLadder.description: Our own ladder, in points, rising with difficulty: open hands built from plain pungs and kongs sit at the bottom (25-40); hands that add flowers, dragons, quints or cross-suit demands sit in the middle (40-55); concealed hands pay more (50-60); concealed singles-and-pairs hands, where no joker can ever help, top the ladder (65-85).

tiers.meaning: exposed with quints, heavy flowers, or tighter structure
concealed singles and pairs — no jokers usable
